verdict.rationale: Buzz lets you mint a separate Nostr keypair per agent as its own credential, distinct from the owner's. Access is scoped through the agent's own channel memberships and audit trail, and NIP-AA ties agent access to the owner's membership so revocation cascades automatically. Community skepticism about the permission model is speculative, not a concrete failure, so it does not create a dispute. missing for 10: fine-grained capability or permission scopes attached to an agent credential (e.g. read-only or per-action limits), expiry or rotation controls, documented least-privilege configuration beyond channel membership, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: Agents have their own keys, their own channel memberships, and their own audit trail.
Running multiple agents? Mint a separate keypair for each.
If the owner's membership is later revoked, the agent's next connection attempt fails automatically — no separate cleanup required.
